ev.q: the risk for cardiac complications was significantly higher after SARS-CoV-2 infection than after mRNA COVID-19 vaccination
Unadjusted RRs and 95% CIs were calculated as the incidences of the outcomes within the infection cohort divided by the incidences
The sex- and age-stratified incidences of the cardiac outcomes (cases per 100,000 persons) were calculated within 7-, 21-, or 42-day risk windows.
Among males aged 5–11 years, the incidences of myocarditis and myocarditis or pericarditis were 12.6–17.6 cases per 100,000 after infection
the risk for cardiac outcomes was 1.8–5.6 times as high after SARS-CoV-2 infection
Cohorts were stratified by sex and age group.
Stratification by age and sex was performed because of their clear prior association with cardiac outcomes.
This study used EHR data from 40 health care systems
Data were obtained through a single query that was executed by participating health care systems to generate aggregated results.

methods_quotes.q: Unadjusted RRs and 95% CIs were calculated as the incidences of the outcomes within the infection cohort divided by the incidences
RRs whose CIs did not include 1.0 were considered statistically significant
RRs were not compared across outcomes, risk windows, vaccine dose, or sex and age stratum.
The sex- and age-stratified incidences of the cardiac outcomes (cases per 100,000 persons) were calculated within 7-, 21-, or 42-day risk windows.
data were obtained using a query that returned aggregate data from sites, precluding adjustment for potential confounders
